notes: Dev ABox revision whose queries carry transitivity and inheritance. Related far: capital_of ⊑ located_in puts Tenochtitlan in the Inca Empire, and located_in is transitive, so the Templo Mayor, stored as standing in Tenochtitlan, stood in the Inca Empire; the step on the edited relation is the subproperty, the step that reaches the temple is transitivity of located_in (hence via located_in). Its original, "the Aztec Templo Mayor", is stored. Risk, recorded: 'Aztec' there names the temple's builders and culture, and a model may answer the Aztec Empire from that attribution; but a model holding the temple in Tenochtitlan and Tenochtitlan in the Inca Empire while putting the temple in the Aztec Empire is inconsistent, not a valid world (README, Determinacy step 3), so the query stays determinate. No landmark of the city is stored without the Aztec label. Related near asks the Inca Empire's capital through the inverse (has_capital): Cusco, stored everywhere, to Tenochtitlan; has_capital is functional, so Cusco is no longer it. The derived queries avoid every fact stored about Tenochtitlan by name. The earlier conquest questions (who conquered the empire whose capital was Tenochtitlan, when it began) and the city's language were dropped: 'Cortés captured Tenochtitlan' (1519-1521) and 'Nahuatl-speaking Tenochtitlan' are stored about the city itself, so Cortés, 1519 and Nahuatl stayed fair answers after the edit. Now two compositions name the Inca Empire as "the empire whose capital was Tenochtitlan" and ask facts stored about the empire only: whether it built Machu Picchu (no, then yes) and its main language (Nahuatl, then Quechua; the language is asked of the empire, not the city, and no firm rule makes an empire's language that of its capital). The third applies the empire's class rule to its new capital (inheritance: the edit gives membership through capital_of ⊑ located_in, the bridge is 'the Inca emperor ruled every city of the Inca Empire'): was Tenochtitlan ruled by the Inca emperor (no, then yes); a model that keeps Moctezuma as the city's ruler still has him under the Inca emperor, so the answer is yes in every world. The city's location on the map is not edited, so no query asks its continent or country (that would split between moving the city and stretching the empire); unrelated near shares the subject: its ruins stay in Mexico in every world. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate.
